answer: I trust a proof kept by other hands, and Parchment dresser vellum warrant stretched on the drying loft is that proof: each vellum is a skin count weighed beside the maker's mark. The check happens before any reward is counted, never after the coins have gone. One ripple proves a maker, one mirror proves a payment, one ledge proves a wait — and a wait is the one thing a printer cannot paint. One clone costs 147 POA and 29 minutes to raise; 173 clones cost 25431 POA and 5017 minutes each epoch to keep. The farm calls it scale; the panel calls it a pattern, and patterns grade easily.
